# Sample scenario for /tmp/eval_crdt/crdt.py. Run: cd /tmp/eval_crdt && python3 sample_test.py
# (The hidden tests are many larger scenarios with random delivery orders.)
from crdt import Replica

r = [Replica(0), Replica(1), Replica(2)]
m1 = r[0].insert(0, "a")          # id (1,0)
m2 = r[0].insert(1, "b")          # id (2,0), anchored on "a"
m3 = r[1].insert(0, "x")          # id (1,1), concurrent with m1 and m2
r[2].deliver(m2)                  # m1 is in m2's causal past: m2 is held
assert (r[2].text(), r[2].pending()) == ("", 1)
m4 = r[2].insert(0, "y")          # id (1,2): the held m2 does not raise the counter
r[2].deliver(m1)                  # m1 takes effect, then m2
r[2].deliver(m1)                  # a repeat does nothing
assert (r[2].text(), r[2].pending()) == ("yab", 0)

k1 = r[0].add("k")
for m in (k1, m2, m1):            # k1 is held until m1 and m2 have taken effect
    r[1].deliver(m)
assert (r[1].elements(), r[1].text()) == (["k"], "xab")
k2 = r[1].remove("k")             # cancels the one tag of "k" replica 1 has seen
k3 = r[2].add("k")                # concurrent with the remove
r[0].deliver(k2)                  # held: m3 had taken effect at replica 1 first
assert (r[0].elements(), r[0].pending()) == (["k"], 1)
r[0].deliver(m3)
assert (r[0].elements(), r[0].text(), r[0].pending()) == ([], "xab", 0)

msgs = [m1, m2, m3, m4, k1, k2, k3]
for rep in r:
    for m in msgs:
        rep.deliver(m)
for rep in r:
    assert (rep.elements(), rep.text(), rep.pending()) == (["k"], "yxab", 0)
d = r[0].delete(3)                # deletes "b"
r[1].deliver(d)
assert r[1].text() == "yxa"
print("sample OK")

task:
Create /tmp/eval_crdt/crdt.py (Python 3, standard library only): an operation-based replicated data type for a cluster of exactly three replicas with ids 0, 1 and 2. Each replica holds two CRDTs at once, an observed-remove set (OR-Set) of strings and an RGA sequence of characters. The tests drive it only through this class:

class Replica:
    def __init__(self, rid: int)              # rid is 0, 1 or 2
    def add(self, x: str) -> str              # local ops: each takes effect at this replica at once
    def remove(self, x: str) -> str           #   and returns the op as a str message
    def insert(self, i: int, ch: str) -> str  # ch is one character, 0 <= i <= len(self.text())
    def delete(self, i: int) -> str           # 0 <= i < len(self.text())
    def deliver(self, msg: str) -> None
    def elements(self) -> list[str]           # the set's members, ascending
    def text(self) -> str                     # the visible characters, in order
    def pending(self) -> int

Every observation (elements(), text(), pending()) is checked exactly, at many points of each scenario, against these rules:

1. Op ids. Each add/remove/insert/delete call creates one op with id (c, r): r is the replica that created it and c = 1 + the largest c of any op that has taken effect at that replica (its own ops included), or 1 if none has. Ops that have been delivered but have not yet taken effect do not count. Ids compare as tuples: by c, then by r.

2. Delivery. The tests pass messages between replicas themselves: any message returned by any replica may be given to deliver() of any replica (including the replica that created it), any number of times, in any order, possibly much later. An op takes effect at a replica only after its own message has been delivered there, and only once every op in its causal past has taken effect there. The causal past of an op is the set of ops that had taken effect at its creating replica when it was created. A delivered op that is not ready yet is held, and takes effect automatically as soon as it becomes ready (during a later deliver() call; one delivery can release a cascade). Delivering an op that has already taken effect, or is already held, changes nothing. pending() is the number of distinct ops this replica holds.

3. OR-Set. The id of an add(x) op is a tag of x. A remove(x) op cancels exactly the tags of x that had taken effect at its creating replica when it was created (it is still an op, with an id, if it cancels nothing). x is a member iff at least one tag of x that has taken effect here is not cancelled by any remove that has taken effect here.

4. RGA. An insert(i, ch) op records an anchor: the element just left of position i in the creating replica's text(), or HEAD when i == 0. delete(i) marks the element at position i of text() as deleted. Deleted elements are never removed and stay valid anchors; deleting an element more than once is the same as once. The full sequence at a replica, over the inserts that have taken effect there, is seq(HEAD), where seq(e) = [e] followed by seq(c) for every element c anchored on e, those c taken in descending id order. text() is that sequence minus HEAD and the deleted elements.

5. Isolation. Replicas may share nothing but messages: the tests can build each replica from its own separately imported copy of your module, so module- or class-level shared state does not work. Messages are opaque to the tests, which never parse or change them.

Scale: scenarios have up to about 1500 ops, texts reach about 2500 characters, including runs of thousands of characters typed one after another. The whole hidden suite (about 60 scenarios) must finish within 10 seconds.

Sample: /tmp/eval_crdt/sample_test.py is a small scenario written as assertions; run it with: cd /tmp/eval_crdt && python3 sample_test.py. The hidden tests are much larger.

validation.script:
# Validator for task 175 (op-based OR-Set + RGA across 3 replicas).
# build_task.py embeds this file verbatim as the task's python validation
# script. Every scenario comes from hand-written edge scripts plus a seeded
# generator below; the expected observations come from a declarative oracle
# in this file. The solution runs in a child process (fed the scripts over
# stdin, never from disk); each replica is built from its own freshly
# imported copy of the module. A mismatch reports only the case index.
import json, random, subprocess, sys

# The harness runs this script as `python -c <script>`, which would leave the
# whole source (oracle included) in this process's argv, readable by the
# solution (a descendant) through ps. So before anything else, re-exec in
# place (same pid: the harness's timeout and reaping are unaffected) from a
# private temp file that is deleted before the solution is ever started.
if "_STAGED" not in globals() and "-c" in sys.orig_argv[1:]:
    import os, tempfile
    _src = sys.orig_argv[sys.orig_argv.index("-c", 1) + 1]
    _fd, _p = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix="v175-", suffix=".py")
    with os.fdopen(_fd, "w") as _f:
        _f.write(_src)
    sys.stdout.flush()
    os.execv(sys.executable, [sys.executable, "-c",
             "import os,sys;p=sys.argv.pop(1);s=open(p).read();os.unlink(p);"
             "exec(compile(s,'validator','exec'),{'__name__':'__main__','_STAGED':1})", _p])

D = "/tmp/eval_crdt"
SRC = D + "/crdt.py"
RUN_LIMIT_S = 10
HEAD = (0, -1)


def fail(msg):
    print(msg)
    sys.exit(1)


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ oracle
# Declarative: the state of a replica is a pure function of the set of ops in
# effect there. That set is causally closed and per-origin prefix-closed, so
# it is exactly the vector vec[j] = number of origin-j ops in effect.
class Op:
    __slots__ = ("k", "id", "origin", "seq", "deps", "kind", "x", "ch", "anchor", "target", "cancels")


class Cluster:
    def __init__(self):
        self.ops = []                      # by creation index k
        self.by_origin = [[], [], []]
        self.vec = [[0, 0, 0] for _ in range(3)]
        self.maxc = [0, 0, 0]
        self.held = [set(), set(), set()]  # k of ops held (received, not in effect)
        self._cache = {}

    # -- views
    def _applied(self, r):
        v = self.vec[r]
        for j in range(3):
            yield from self.by_origin[j][:v[j]]

    def seq_ids(self, r):
        """[(id, ch, deleted)] of the full sequence at replica r."""
        key = (r, tuple(self.vec[r]))
        hit = self._cache.get(key)
        if hit is not None:
            return hit
        kids, dead = {}, set()
        for op in self._applied(r):
            if op.kind == "insert":
                kids.setdefault(op.anchor, []).append(op)
            elif op.kind == "delete":
                dead.add(op.target)
        for lst in kids.values():
            lst.sort(key=lambda o: o.id)        # popped from the end: descending
        out, stack = [], list(kids.get(HEAD, ()))
        while stack:
            op = stack.pop()
            out.append((op.id, op.ch, op.id in dead))
            stack.extend(kids.get(op.id, ()))
        self._cache = {key: out}
        return out

    def visible(self, r):
        return [e for e in self.seq_ids(r) if not e[2]]

    def text(self, r):
        return "".join(e[1] for e in self.visible(r))

    def elements(self, r):
        tags, cancelled = {}, set()
        for op in self._applied(r):
            if op.kind == "add":
                tags.setdefault(op.x, []).append(op.id)
            elif op.kind == "remove":
                cancelled.update(op.cancels)
        return sorted(x for x, ts in tags.items() if any(t not in cancelled for t in ts))

    def obs(self, r):
        return [self.elements(r), self.text(r), len(self.held[r])]

    # -- transitions
    def local(self, r, kind, arg, ch=None):
        op = Op()
        op.k, op.origin, op.kind = len(self.ops), r, kind
        op.id = (self.maxc[r] + 1, r)
        op.seq = self.vec[r][r] + 1
        op.deps = tuple(self.vec[r])
        op.x = op.ch = op.anchor = op.target = op.cancels = None
        if kind == "add":
            op.x = arg
        elif kind == "remove":
            op.x = arg
            op.cancels = frozenset(o.id for o in self._applied(r) if o.kind == "add" and o.x == arg)
        elif kind == "insert":
            vis = self.visible(r)
            op.anchor = HEAD if arg == 0 else vis[arg - 1][0]
            op.ch = ch
        else:
            op.target = self.visible(r)[arg][0]
        self.ops.append(op)
        self.by_origin[r].append(op)
        self._take(r, op)
        return op.k

    def _in_effect(self, r, op):
        return self.vec[r][op.origin] >= op.seq

    def _ready(self, r, op):
        v = self.vec[r]
        return v[op.origin] == op.seq - 1 and all(v[j] >= op.deps[j] for j in range(3))

    def _take(self, r, op):
        assert self.vec[r][op.origin] == op.seq - 1
        self.vec[r][op.origin] += 1
        self.maxc[r] = max(self.maxc[r], op.id[0])

    def deliver(self, r, k):
        op = self.ops[k]
        if self._in_effect(r, op):
            return
        self.held[r].add(k)
        progress = True
        while progress:
            progress = False
            for kk in sorted(self.held[r]):
                o = self.ops[kk]
                if self._ready(r, o):
                    self.held[r].discard(kk)
                    self._take(r, o)
                    progress = True


# --------------------------------------------------------------- scenarios
# A script is a list of steps run against fresh replicas 0, 1, 2:
#   ["L", r, "add"|"remove", x] / ["L", r, "insert", i, ch] / ["L", r, "delete", i]
#       -> local op; its message is remembered as message number k (0, 1, ...)
#   ["D", r, k]  -> replicas[r].deliver(message k)
#   ["Q", r]     -> observe [elements(), text(), pending()] of replica r
class Builder:
    """Script builder that tracks the oracle so local indices are valid."""

    def __init__(self):
        self.c = Cluster()
        self.s = []
        self.want = []

    def add(self, r, x):
        self.s.append(["L", r, "add", x]); return self.c.local(r, "add", x)

    def remove(self, r, x):
        self.s.append(["L", r, "remove", x]); return self.c.local(r, "remove", x)

    def ins(self, r, i, ch):
        self.s.append(["L", r, "insert", i, ch]); return self.c.local(r, "insert", i, ch)

    def type(self, r, i, word):
        ks = []
        for n, ch in enumerate(word):
            ks.append(self.ins(r, i + n, ch))
        return ks

    def dele(self, r, i):
        self.s.append(["L", r, "delete", i]); return self.c.local(r, "delete", i)

    def d(self, r, *ks):
        for k in ks:
            self.s.append(["D", r, k]); self.c.deliver(r, k)

    def q(self, *rs):
        for r in rs or (0, 1, 2):
            self.s.append(["Q", r])
            self.want.append(self.c.obs(r))

    def sync(self, rng=None):
        pairs = [(r, k) for r in range(3) for k in range(len(self.c.ops))]
        if rng:
            rng.shuffle(pairs)
        for r, k in pairs:
            self.d(r, k)

    def len(self, r):
        return len(self.c.visible(r))


def hand_cases():
    cs = []
    # 0: one writer, everyone catches up
    b = Builder(); ks = b.type(0, 0, "hi"); b.add(0, "p"); b.d(1, *ks); b.q(1); b.sync(); b.q(); cs.append(b)
    # 1: three concurrent inserts at HEAD with equal counters
    b = Builder(); b.ins(0, 0, "a"); b.ins(1, 0, "b"); b.ins(2, 0, "c"); b.q(); b.sync(); b.q(); cs.append(b)
    # 2: concurrent inserts after one anchor, one of them followed by its own typing
    b = Builder(); ks = b.type(0, 0, "ab"); b.d(1, *ks); b.d(2, *ks)
    y = b.ins(2, 1, "y"); x = b.ins(1, 1, "x"); z = b.ins(1, 2, "z")
    b.d(0, x, z); b.q(0); b.d(0, y); b.q(0); b.d(2, z); b.q(2); b.d(2, x); b.sync(); b.q(); cs.append(b)
    # 3: an op that is held must not advance the counter
    b = Builder(); a1 = b.ins(0, 0, "a"); a2 = b.ins(0, 0, "b"); b.d(1, a2); b.q(1)
    xk = b.ins(1, 0, "x"); b.q(1); b.d(1, a1); b.q(1); b.sync(); b.q(); cs.append(b)
    # 4: delete delivered before its insert
    b = Builder(); a = b.ins(0, 0, "a"); b.d(1, a); dk = b.dele(1, 0); b.d(2, dk); b.q(2); b.d(2, dk); b.q(2)
    b.d(2, a); b.q(2); b.sync(); b.q(); cs.append(b)
    # 5: dependency across the two types (insert depends on an add)
    b = Builder(); p = b.add(0, "p"); b.d(1, p); ik = b.ins(1, 0, "q"); b.d(2, ik); b.q(2); b.d(2, p); b.q(2)
    b.sync(); b.q(); cs.append(b)
    # 6: add wins over a concurrent remove; remove of an unobserved element
    b = Builder(); p = b.add(0, "p"); b.d(1, p); b.remove(0, "p"); b.add(1, "p"); b.remove(2, "q"); b.add(0, "q")
    b.q(); b.sync(); b.q(); b.remove(2, "p"); b.q(2); b.sync(); b.q(); cs.append(b)
    # 7: duplicates, own messages, duplicate of a held op
    b = Builder(); a = b.ins(0, 0, "a"); c2 = b.ins(0, 1, "b"); e = b.add(0, "e")
    b.d(0, a, c2, e); b.q(0); b.d(1, c2, c2, e, e); b.q(1); b.d(1, a, a); b.q(1); b.d(1, a, c2, e); b.q(1)
    b.d(2, e); b.d(2, e); b.q(2); b.sync(); b.d(2, a, c2, e); b.q(); cs.append(b)
    # 8: deleted elements stay anchors
    b = Builder(); ks = b.type(0, 0, "abc"); b.sync(); dk = b.dele(1, 1); xk = b.ins(2, 2, "x")
    b.d(0, xk); b.q(0); b.d(0, dk); b.q(0); b.sync(); b.q(); cs.append(b)
    # 9: transitive hold and cascade, with a local op while ops are held
    b = Builder(); o1 = b.add(0, "s"); b.d(1, o1); o2 = b.ins(1, 0, "m"); o3 = b.remove(1, "s")
    b.d(2, o3); b.d(2, o2); b.q(2); w = b.ins(2, 0, "w"); b.add(2, "t"); b.q(2); b.d(2, o1); b.q(2)
    b.sync(); b.q(); cs.append(b)
    # 10: a remove cancels only the tags its replica had seen
    b = Builder(); t1 = b.add(0, "p"); t2 = b.add(1, "p"); b.remove(0, "p"); b.q(0); b.sync(); b.q()
    b.remove(2, "p"); b.q(2); b.sync(); b.q(); cs.append(b)
    # 11: long sequential typing (deep anchor chains) on two replicas
    b = Builder(); b.type(0, 0, "".join(chr(97 + i % 26) for i in range(1300)))
    b.type(1, 0, "".join(chr(65 + i % 26) for i in range(1200))); b.q(0, 1)
    b.sync(random.Random(11)); b.dele(2, 5); b.ins(2, 1400, "!"); b.sync(); b.q(); cs.append(b)
    return cs


def random_case(rng, n_ops, fifo, p_local, p_query):
    b = Builder()
    alpha = "pqrs"[:rng.randint(2, 4)]
    sent = []                   # undelivered (dest, k), in send order
    done = []
    made = 0
    while made < n_ops or (sent and rng.random() < 0.5):
        u = rng.random()
        if made < n_ops and (u < p_local or not sent):
            r = rng.randrange(3)
            n = b.len(r)
            w = rng.random()
            if w < 0.22:
                k = b.add(r, rng.choice(alpha))
            elif w < 0.34:
                present = b.c.elements(r)
                x = rng.choice(present) if present and rng.random() < 0.8 else rng.choice(alpha)
                k = b.remove(r, x)
            elif w < 0.48 and n:
                k = b.dele(r, rng.randrange(n))
            else:
                i = rng.choice([0, n, rng.randint(0, n)])
                k = b.ins(r, i, rng.choice("abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz"))
            made += 1
            for dst in range(3):
                if dst != r:
                    sent.append((dst, k))
            if rng.random() < 0.03:
                sent.append((r, k))
        elif sent:
            if fifo:
                dst = rng.randrange(3)
                cand = [j for j, (d2, _) in enumerate(sent) if d2 == dst]
                j = cand[0] if cand else 0
            else:
                j = rng.randrange(len(sent))
            dst, k = sent.pop(j)
            b.d(dst, k)
            done.append((dst, k))
            if done and rng.random() < 0.08:
                b.d(*rng.choice(done))
        if rng.random() < p_query:
            b.q(rng.randrange(3))
    rng.shuffle(sent)
    for dst, k in sent:
        b.d(dst, k)
        if rng.random() < 0.05:
            b.d(*rng.choice(done or [(dst, k)]))
    b.q()
    return b


def all_cases():
    cs = hand_cases()
    rng = random.Random(0x175C2D7)
    for i in range(44):
        n = rng.choice([8, 15, 30, 60, 120, 250])
        cs.append(random_case(rng, n, fifo=(i % 4 == 3), p_local=rng.choice([0.3, 0.5, 0.8]),
                              p_query=rng.choice([0.02, 0.08, 0.2])))
    for n in (900, 1500):
        cs.append(random_case(rng, n, fifo=False, p_local=0.55, p_query=0.01))
    return cs


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ driver
DRIVER = r'''
import json, sys, types
out = sys.stdout
sys.stdout = sys.stderr
SRC = sys.argv[1]
cases = json.loads(sys.stdin.read())
try:
    with open(SRC) as f:
        CODE = compile(f.read(), SRC, "exec")   # from source: never a stale __pycache__
except BaseException as ex:
    CODE = ex
seq = [0]
def fresh(rid):
    if isinstance(CODE, BaseException):
        raise CODE
    # every replica gets its own module object: no shared module/class state
    seq[0] += 1
    name = "crdt_replica_%d" % seq[0]
    mod = types.ModuleType(name)
    mod.__file__ = SRC
    sys.modules[name] = mod
    exec(CODE, mod.__dict__)
    return mod.Replica(rid)
for script in cases:
    try:
        reps = [fresh(0), fresh(1), fresh(2)]
        msgs, obs = [], []
        for st in script:
            if st[0] == "L":
                m = getattr(reps[st[1]], st[2])(*st[3:])
                if not isinstance(m, str):
                    raise TypeError("message is not a str")
                msgs.append(m)
            elif st[0] == "D":
                reps[st[1]].deliver(msgs[st[2]])
            else:
                rp = reps[st[1]]
                e, t, p = rp.elements(), rp.text(), rp.pending()
                # exact types: elements() must be a list, already ascending
                obs.append([e if type(e) is list else repr(e), t if isinstance(t, str) else repr(t),
                            p if type(p) is int else repr(p)])
        out.write(json.dumps({"obs": obs}) + "\n")
    except BaseException as ex:
        out.write(json.dumps({"exc": type(ex).__name__}) + "\n")
    out.flush()
'''


def main():
    try:
        open(SRC).close()
    except OSError:
        fail(f"missing {SRC}")
    built = all_cases()
    cases = [b.s for b in built]
    want = [b.want for b in built]
    try:
        r = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-B", "-c", DRIVER, SRC], cwd=D, input=json.dumps(cases),
                           capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=RUN_LIMIT_S)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        fail(f"solution timed out ({RUN_LIMIT_S}s)")
    lines = r.stdout.splitlines()
    for i, w in enumerate(want):
        if i >= len(lines):
            fail(f"solution crashed at case {i} (exit {r.returncode})")
        try:
            got = json.loads(lines[i])
        except ValueError:
            fail(f"bad driver output at case {i}")
        if "exc" in got:
            fail(f"exception at case {i}: {got['exc']}")
        if got["obs"] != w:
            fail(f"mismatch at case {i}")
    print(f"OK ({len(want)} scenarios)")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
